description:
As a container specialist managing microservices, you need to automate the process of checking the status of three service containers: "api_service", "web_service", and "db_service". 

Please write a shell command that outputs the status of each service container. The output must follow this exact format for each service (one line per service):

Service: <service_name> | Status: <status>

Where:
- <service_name> is the name of the service as listed above.
- <status> is either "running", "stopped", or "not_found" depending on whether the container process is currently running, not running, or does not exist.

The status check should look for containers started by docker, podman, or apptainer, if any are available on the system.

The output should be written into a file located at /home/user/service_status_report.txt. The file should contain a total of three lines, in this exact order:
1. Service: api_service | Status: <status>
2. Service: web_service | Status: <status>
3. Service: db_service | Status: <status>

If a container engine is not installed or none of the services are found, the status for each should be "not_found".

Please do not include any additional information or formatting. The file /home/user/service_status_report.txt should be overwritten with new results each time the command is run.
truth:
Before the task begins, no file at /home/user/service_status_report.txt exists.

After execution, /home/user/service_status_report.txt must exist, owned by user:user with 644 permissions.

Sample contents of /home/user/service_status_report.txt after correct status checks (if all three containers are not found):

Service: api_service | Status: not_found
Service: web_service | Status: not_found
Service: db_service | Status: not_found

If api_service is running and web_service is stopped (exists but not running), with db_service not found, the file should contain:

Service: api_service | Status: running
Service: web_service | Status: stopped
Service: db_service | Status: not_found

The file must always contain exactly three lines, one for each service listed in the specified order.
